title: Canary slice selection and guardrails notes (working)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the pragmatic rules-of-thumb and operational guardrails for selecting canary slices and running short A/B experiments across product, infra, and SRE. Focus: choose slices that reveal correctness and performance regressions quickly while minimizing blast radius. This is intentionally an operational memo — not final policy.

Scope / when to use these notes:
- Small code or model changes that affect inference path (runtime, kernel selection, minor tokenization fixes)
- Config changes that influence batching, caching, or routing decisions
- Feature flags that change API surface or response shape (e.g., structured output toggles)
- NOT for major model upgrades or infra topology changes that require Dedicated/Private migration runbooks

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Choose 3 orthogonal slices: pre-validated internal traffic, synthetic-heavy test slice, and 1 small external customer slice (<=1% active users).
- Monitor three dimensions in first 15m: correctness (error rate/regression), latency (p50/p95), and cost (tokens/sec and GPU util).
- Abort if any guardrail breach persists >5m after triage and mitigation attempt.

Roles & coordination:
- Product (owner): define experiment objective, expected user-visible change, primary correctness metric.
- Eng (owner): deploy canary, ensure telemetry hooks, own rollback automation.
- SRE: configure emergency circuit-breakers, synthetic load targets, and runbook on-call support.
- Solutions/CS: select customer slice and coordinate communication risk.
- Privacy/Legal (optional): if new output shape impacts PII, consult before canary.

Slice selection rubric (notes + examples):
- Internal telemetry slice (mandatory): 0.5% of internal API keys or a "canary-internal" header. Purpose: catch obvious regressions early with zero external customer impact.
- Synthetic workload slice (mandatory): hit the service with a curated prompt set (short/long sequences, edge cases). Always run alongside internal slice for performance assertions.
- External small customer slice (optional but recommended for user-facing changes): select opt-in customers or low-traffic customers. Max size: 0.5%–1% of active requests for first hour.
- Geographical diversity: if feature is region-specific, include a representative region slice (do not combine region + customer slice in first stage).
- Device/channel diversity: where relevant, ensure at least one mobile and one web client represented in slices.

Slice selection heuristics (what to avoid):
- Avoid picking any customer already on a Premium SLA plan or any customer with manual routing restrictions without explicit consent.
- Avoid slices that depend on seasonal spikes (e.g., billing-run traffic) unless experiment targets that workload.

Metrics (primary + safety):
Primary correctness metrics (product-defined):
- Regression rate on deterministic assertions (% failed unit checks) — expected baseline and tolerance e.g., <0.5% absolute lift.
- Semantic quality delta measured via existing eval harness (BLEU-ish or model QA pass rate)
Safety / platform metrics (SRE):
- p50/p90/p95 latency change vs baseline (alert if p95 increases >25% or absolute exceeds 1200 ms for text-gen endpoints).
- Error rate (4xx/5xx) — alert if sustained >2x baseline or absolute >0.5% for 5m.
- GPU util and queue growth — alert if per-host queue length doubling or GPU util >95% for >3min.
- Cost signals: tokens/sec and inference-cost-per-token — note sudden increases ( >20%).
- Cache hit rate (if change affects caching) — monitor drop >10pp.

Observability checklist (pre-canary):
- Dashboards: ensure the canary slice has its own dashboard tile (latency, errors, traffic volume, GPU util)
- Traces: sampling rules and alerting for high error traces enabled
- Log tagging: add "canary_id" header to logs and traces
- Canary-specific SLOs: create temporary SLO window (first 60m) with tighter alerting thresholds
- Synthetic runner: scheduled job running curated prompts every 30s, results pushed to monitoring channel

Ramp plan (example sequence):
1) Warm-up (0 min): deploy canary to 0% traffic, warm caches with synthetic runner (5–15 min).
2) Internal soak (15 min): send 0.5% internal traffic + synthetic runner. Validate correctness and performance.
3) Micro ramp (30–60 min): increase external slice to 0.1% for 10–15 min, observe.
4) Small ramp (next 60–120 min): increase to 0.5–1% if stable.
5) Observe & decide: after reaching 1% stable for 1h with no regressions, move to broader rollout or to A/B for feature effect measurement.

Abort / rollback criteria (operational):
- Immediate rollback triggers (no triage): fatal errors (service crash, panic), large memory leaks, or data corruption signs.
- Conditional rollback triggers (triage + 5m):
  * p95 latency > 2x baseline or >2000 ms for >5 minutes
  * Error rate > 1% absolute increase sustained for 5 minutes
  * Synthetic regression failing >50% of curated correctness assertions
  * GPU queuing indications: queue length growth >2x baseline and growing
- Communication: owner must post to #rollouts on Slack with status and decision within 5 minutes of abort decision.

A/B test notes (when to convert canary -> A/B):
- If product goal is to measure user behavior change (engagement, conversion), convert to A/B only after canary stability criteria met for performance and correctness.
- Randomization point: try to randomize at request or user-id depending on metric to avoid leakage; maintain consistent exposure for returning sessions for at least 24h.
- Minimum sample sizing: calculate powered test (baseline conversion rate, delta) — but start with minimal safe volume (>=1% users) for non-critical metrics.

Post-canary analysis template (what to capture):
- Time window and traffic volumes by slice
- Primary metric deltas (with confidence intervals where possible)
- Platform metric deltas (latency distribution, error breakdown, GPU util, queue metrics)
- Notable traces and example failing prompts (redact PII)
- Actions taken (rollback, fix, patch) and time to remediation
- Decision: promote / increase / rollback / repeat with tweak

Open questions / TODOs:
- SHOULD we require explicit customer consent for ANY external slice? (product/legal to decide)
- Define canonical canary header name across teams — currently some services use X-Canary, others use x-exp. Proposal: X-RW-Canary. (TODO: eng infra to finalize)
- Consensus on threshold windows: 5m vs 15m for different classes of failures. (SRE suggestion: fatal=0min, perf=5m, correctness=15m)
- Automate synthetic runner registration into dashboards (Samir to prototype)

Runbook snippets (copy/paste for on-call):
- Check dashboard "Canary quick view" -> look at error spikes and p95 -> if p95 spike, tail-sample traces -> if trace points to change, initiate rollback with /rollback-canary <id>
- If error 500s: look for stack traces tagged with canary_id -> if unknown, escalate to eng-owner

Communication & stakeholder playbook:
- Pre-canary: owners post experiment plan to #rollouts and tag SRE + CS 24h in advance for external slices
- During canary: live updates every 15 min to #rollouts; immediate ping on abort
- Post-canary: short summary doc in Confluence with metrics and decision; inform affected customers if needed

Examples (realistic toy cases):
- Tokenizer tweak: internal slice detects 0.8% assertion regression -> rollback immediately; follow-up fix and re-run synthetic runner until green.
- Batching policy change: initial micro ramp shows p95 increase by 40% due to longer pack time -> SRE reduces batch window and re-tests.

Appendix: canned checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Owner assigned and slack channel noted
- [ ] Canary header added and tagged in logs
- [ ] Synthetic runner healthy and dashboard connected
- [ ] Canaries in region(s) required configured
- [ ] External customer slice size agreed and customers notified if applicable
- [ ] Alert thresholds set and tested
- [ ] Rollback automation tested in staging

Notes-to-self / brain dump (scratchpad):
- We should try a single signal derived from model-likelihood anomalies to surface hallucination drift quickly. Hard to get right, but could be a high-signal, low-volume early-warning.
- Consider low-latency shadowing of outputs for a tiny % to a quality-check pipeline with human-in-loop for high-risk customers.

Next steps (owners):
- Evan: prototype X-RW-Canary header enforcement and log tagging (ETA: 2 weeks)
- Samir: synthetic-runner -> dashboard plumbing (ETA: 3 weeks)
- Leah: draft customer notification template for opt-in external slices (ETA: 1 week)
- Aisha: consolidate feedback and propose final guardrail doc for review (ETA: end of month)

-- end --
